Article Title: How Jantar Mantar became Delhi's designated protest site and what changes now
Article Text:
Jantar Mantar’s changing role in Delhi’s history of dissent

Jantar Mantar’s legacy: A landmark site of dissent faces a shift

Before Jantar Mantar, there was Boat Club

When Rajpath became a protest ground

How Jantar Mantar became Delhi's protest address

When the right to protest reached the Supreme Court

What changes now?

Why the location of a protest matters

NEW DELHI: Jantar Mantar, one of Delhi's best-known protest venues, has lost its status as a designated site for demonstrations. On October 12, Delhi Police de-notified the site and named three alternatives: Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi.The decision follows recommendations from a committee constituted by the ministry of home affairs (MHA) to examine alternative venues for protests and demonstrations.For several decades, Jantar Mantar has been synonymous with protests in the national capital, a place where farmers, students, workers and political organisations have gathered to raise their demands.However, Delhi's address for protests has not always been Jantar Mantar. Before it emerged as a prominent hub for demonstrations, the sprawling lawns around India Gate and the Boat Club, close to Parliament and the government's principal offices, were among the capital's most important spaces for political mobilisation.The latest decision marks another chapter in the history of how authorities have regulated where citizens can assemble to make their voices heard.For decades after Independence, the Boat Club lawns near India Gate were an important venue for political rallies.The lawns near modern-day Central Vista gave demonstrators proximity to Parliament, the government's principal offices and other institutions at the centre of national power.The scale of the gatherings, however, also presented challenges for the authorities.One of the defining episodes came in 1988, when farmer leader Mahendra Singh Tikait led a massive agitation in Delhi. Farmers gathered at the Boat Club and surrounding lawns to press their demands, bringing a large mobilisation into the heart of the capital.The episode became a turning point in the debate over whether such prominent public spaces should remain open to large demonstrations.Authorities increasingly sought to regulate gatherings in central Delhi, citing concerns around security, traffic and public order.In 'India After Gandhi: The History of the World's Largest Democracy', historian Ramachandra Guha recounts how the lawns along present-day Kartavya Path, formerly Rajpath and known as Kingsway during British rule, became a prominent site of political dissent in the early 1990s.The book recalls tents occupied by people from different parts of the country, representing causes ranging from demands for a separate state and better prices for agricultural produce to recognition for regional languages.Other groups included industrial workers, Tibetan refugees seeking Indian citizenship and Hindu religious organisations campaigning on cow slaughter.The lawns near the country's most prominent government buildings in Lutyens' Delhi became a temporary home for movements that wanted their demands to be seen and heard.But the encampments did not last. Guha writes that the tents were dismantled in the early 1990s, with the government concerned about the impression created by visible demonstrations near the ceremonial heart of the capital.Protesters subsequently regrouped near Jantar Mantar, where they remained visible to people passing through the busy commercial district.The restrictions on gatherings around Boat Club and Rajpath helped set the stage for Jantar Mantar's emergence as a prominent location for demonstrations.Built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II in the 18th century, Delhi's Jantar Mantar is an open-air astronomical observatory designed to track celestial movements.Over time, the area around the historic site evolved into a major hub for protest movements, offering demonstrators a prominent public platform while remaining easier to manage than larger, more central locations.Located close to busy Connaught Place and within reach of Parliament and government offices, it allowed demonstrators to bring their demands into public view without occupying the expansive lawns around India Gate.The site hosted protests involving workers, farmers, civil society groups and citizens campaigning on a range of social and political issues.Its prominence grew further during the anti-corruption movement led by social activist Anna Hazare in 2011, when demonstrations demanding a stronger Lokpal mechanism brought corruption and accountability to the centre of national political debate.As the movement grew, Ramlila Maidan became the venue for larger gatherings and Hazare's prolonged fast. The two locations demonstrated how different sites in Delhi could accommodate protests of different scales.The significance of Jantar Mantar was not simply a matter of geography. It became an established public address for people seeking to draw the attention of political leaders, government officials and the media to their grievances.Over the years, Jantar Mantar has witnessed protests on a range of issues, from Anna Hazare's campaign for a Lokpal Bill and the 2017 Tamil Nadu farmers' agitation to demonstrations against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act and the wrestlers' protests against Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh in 2023.More recently, it became the centre of demonstrations by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over the NEET paper leak and demands for the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.However, its status as a designated protest venue did not mean that demonstrations could take place without restrictions. Police permissions, public-order measures and court directions continued to determine how the site could be used.In October 2017, the National Green Tribunal (NGT) ordered an end to protests at Jantar Mantar following complaints about noise, sanitation and disruption to residents.The restrictions were subsequently challenged before the Supreme Court.In its July 23, 2018, judgment in Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan v Union of India, the Supreme Court examined restrictions on protests at Jantar Mantar and the Boat Club, including the effects of demonstrations on residents and public spaces.The court recognised peaceful assembly and protest as fundamental rights under Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(b) of the Constitution. At the same time, it acknowledged that the exercise of these rights could be regulated to protect public order and the interests of other citizens.The judgment addressed the competing claims of demonstrators and residents, making clear that one group's rights could not simply extinguish those of another.It called for a balance between the right to protest and the need to prevent unreasonable disruption.The constitutional basis for that balance is set out in Article 19. Article 19(1)(b) guarantees citizens the right to assemble peacefully and without arms, while Article 19(3) permits reasonable restrictions in the interests of the sovereignty and integrity of India or public order.The latest decision comes amid protests by opposition parties and the youth-led CJP against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The proposed CJP protest on October 10 was met with extensive security arrangements, detentions and restrictions on movement in parts of Delhi.Under the new arrangement, Jantar Mantar will no longer be a designated protest venue. Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi have been identified as alternatives.Delhi Police has said a detailed and revised standard operating procedure for demonstrations at these three venues will be issued separately.The decision changes where organisers can hold demonstrations under the designated-venue system. However, de-notification should not be confused with a blanket prohibition on all peaceful assembly, which remains subject to constitutional protections and lawful restrictions.The significance of the decision extends beyond the physical relocation of demonstrations. The location of a protest affects its visibility, the ease with which people can reach it and its proximity to the institutions being addressed.A venue in central Delhi offers demonstrators a different kind of access and public visibility from a ground farther away from the corridors of power.For organisers, the choice of location can therefore be an important part of how a protest communicates its message.Among the newly designated venues, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi are farther from the central government district than Jantar Mantar.At the same time, large demonstrations in central Delhi can create challenges for traffic management, security and the daily movement of residents.The October 10 protests, for instance, were accompanied by extensive security arrangements and disruptions to movement across parts of the city.The latest decision once again brings into focus a question that has shaped Delhi's protest history for decades: how to balance the right to peaceful demonstrations with security, public order and the functioning of the national capital.
Article Summary: Delhi Police de-notified Jantar Mantar on October 12. Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi have been named as alternatives. The decision follows recommendations from a committee constituted by the ministry of home affairs.

Article Title: 'Don't pick up words like this': SC says neither approved nor disapproved new Form 6, to examine its validity
Article Text:
The revised declaration has come under scrutiny over changes introduced by the Election Commission.

What is Form 6 controversy

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday stated that it had neither approved nor disapproved the new Form 6 declaration used for voter registration, saying it had not adjudicated on its validity and would examine the issue.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana made the oral observations while hearing a writ petition concerning the functioning of the Election Commission of India (EC) and changes to voter registration forms.Form 6 is the application through which an eligible person seeks inclusion in the electoral roll.During the hearing, advocate Narendra Mishra, appearing for the petitioner, referred to the Election Commission's claim that the Supreme Court had approved the new Form 6 declaration."There is no adjudication on the new Form 6," Justice Bagchi said, clarifying that the court had only observed that the new form was not in existence when it delivered its judgment on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Bihar in May 2026."What the Hon'ble Chief Justice said was that when the Bihar SIR judgment was delivered, new Form 6 was not there. That does not either say it is approved or disapproved by the Supreme Court.We will examine it," Justice Bagchi said, according to LiveLaw.The Chief Justice cautioned lawyers against reading too much into the court's observations, saying, "Don't pick up words like this ..."The bench agreed to issue notice on the petition and listed the matter for October 27 along with connected petitions concerning Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The new Form 6 declaration has become controversial following allegations that changes were introduced into the voter registration process without following the prescribed legal procedure.Under the revised declaration, applicants seeking registration as new voters are required to state whether they or their parents were mapped in the previous SIR. The earlier Form 6 used during electoral roll revisions in other states did not seek such a declaration.The controversy intensified after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected to the changes, arguing that the form could not be modified without an amendment to the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, by the Central government.On September 26, the Election Commission issued a press release suggesting that the Supreme Court had upheld the new Form 6 declaration in its May 2026 judgment concerning the Bihar SIR.However, the Supreme Court clarified on October 5 that it had not approved modifications to Form 6.
Article Summary: Supreme Court says it has not adjudicated on the validity of the new Form 6 declaration. The new declaration has come under scrutiny over changes introduced by the Election Commission. The Chief Justice cautioned lawyers against reading too much into the court's observations, saying, "Don't pick up words like this..."

Article Title: Why CJI declined to meet Rahul Gandhi, Kharge amid protests against Gyanesh Kumar
Article Text:
CJI Suryakant, Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge

NEW DELHI: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant had declined a request from Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi and Rajya Sabha leader of opposition Mallikarjun Kharge for a meeting to discuss issues arising from the ongoing protests in Delhi.He said the matters are already pending before the Supreme Court and discussing them administratively would violate the principle of separation of powers.In a letter dated October 11, the CJI advised the two Opposition leaders to approach the Supreme Court through the judicial process instead of submitting a memorandum on the administrative side. He also assured them that any petition filed on the issues would be heard at the earliest possible opportunity in accordance with the law.The request concerned allegations of irregularities involving the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and the Election Commission of India, alleged arbitrary arrests of students, the closure of metro stations and the cancellation of trains amid protests in the national capital.Explaining his decision, CJI Surya Kant said the issues raised by Gandhi and Kharge were “already sub judice before the Supreme Court of India .”“Therefore, convening a meeting to discuss pending cases would wholly contravene the principle of Separation of Powers, an intrinsic facet of the basic structure doctrine of the Constitution of India, and would be incompatible with the established ethics and judicial propriety,” the CJI said.He also clarified that the Supreme Court did not have administrative powers to address the concerns raised in their letter, but could examine them through its judicial jurisdiction.“However, in the exercise of our jurisdiction under Article 32 of our Constitution, along with other plenary powers, including that of judicial review, we are duty-bound to consider on the judicial side the gravamen of issues affecting the citizens of India,” he said.The CJI reiterated the Supreme Court’s commitment to protecting citizens’ fundamental rights and said they could seek their enforcement through the legal process.“Supreme Court of India reiterates its commitment to preserve and protect the Fundamental Rights of every citizen of India and they are entitled to seek enforcement of such rights at all hours through the procedure known in law. It would thus be more appropriate on your part to invoke the judicial powers of the Supreme Court of India, instead of submitting a memorandum on the administrative side,” he said.Pointing to the court’s schedule, CJI Surya Kant said matters involving similar issues were listed for hearing on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. He invited the Opposition leaders to file a petition on Monday, either physically or through the court’s e-filing facility.“If so advised, you may submit your petition on Monday, either physically at the Supreme Court of India, between 10:30 A.M. and 04:30 P.M., or alternatively, by utilising the e-filing option, which permits filing at any time and on any day. You have my assurance that any such petition shall be heard at the earliest possible opportunity, in accordance with the law,” he said.Gandhi and Kharge had sought an appointment with the CJI amid Opposition protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of electoral irregularities, including what Congress has described as “vote chori”.Kharge said in a social media post on Sunday that the Opposition would continue its fight and that he and Gandhi had written to the CJI seeking a meeting.“We will continue our fight. Tomorrow, we are also going to meet CJI. I have written a letter, and Rahul Gandhi has also written a letter. We have scheduled a meeting between 4-5pm, during which we will apprise him of the situation... Chaos is being created in the country by home minister and PM, and everywhere an undeclared emergency is imposed,” Kharge said.The CJI’s response leaves the Opposition leaders free to pursue their concerns through a formal petition, with the court indicating that related matters could be taken up through judicial proceedings.
Article Summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant declined a request from Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge for a meeting to discuss issues. He said the matters are already pending before the Supreme Court and discussing them administratively would violate the principle of separation of powers. Gandhi and Kharge had sought an appointment with the CJI amid Opposition protests.

CHENNAI: PM Narendra Modi inaugurated and laid the foundation for infrastructure projects worth Rs 13,000 crore in Chennai Sunday, promising Centre's support for Tamil Nadu's growth, as CM C Joseph Vijay sought funds while navigating ties with BJP-led Union govt and ally Congress."We are taking Tamil Nadu's development journey forward with CM Vijay," Modi said at IIT Madras, adding that the projects spanning Chennai Metro , roads, railways & ports would generate direct and indirect jobs. "Let us create a developed India through a developed Tamil Nadu," he said.Modi recalled his association with former Tamil Nadu CMs M Karunanidhi, J Jayalalithaa, O Panneerselvam, Edappadi K Palaniswami and MK Stalin, saying his commitment to the state remained steadfast despite changes in govt.Vijay, who hosted MP Rahul Gandhi at his home less than 24 hours earlier, shared a Metro ride and stage with Modi, signalling his intent to maintain working ties with Centre while preserving TVK's partnership with Congress. They travelled on the first driverless metro train from Porur Bypass to Poonamallee Bypass and back.This marked the first time Modi and Vijay shared a stage and the CM's first meeting with Rahul since TVK joined INDIA bloc.BJP spokesperson Narayanan Tirupathy welcomed Vijay's engagement with Modi. "He was very cordial with the PM. This is what people of Tamil Nadu want and this is what would help the state grow," Tirupathy said.Congress neta A Gopanna said the two meetings served different purposes. He thanked Modi for announcing high-speed networks connecting Chennai with Hyderabad and Bengaluru in the Budget.At the golden jubilee event of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya Matriculation Higher Secondary School at Chennai Trade Centre, Modi urged students to dream big and act fearlessly. He cited India's ambitions of becoming one of the world's largest economies. "This is your time. This is your opportunity," he told students.

Article Title: India’s agri-seed sector accounts for the largest share of receipts under benefit sharing regulations during April-Sept
Article Text:
ABS mechanism goes beyond monetary collection by linking the utilisation of biological resources with biodiversity conservation,

NEW DELHI: India’s agri-seed sector accounted for the largest share of receipts from users of the country’s biological resources during April-Sept period this financial year under the Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) regulation -- a statutory mechanism which ensures that when local genetic resources create commercial value, a fair share flows back to states and communities to sustain that diversity.Though the amount of little over Rs 7 crore for the sector during that six-month period is not much, the receipts, at least, reflect working of the ABS mechanism in generating money by getting payment for utilisation of a diverse range of biological resources across agriculture sector.The other sectors that generate receipts include food, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, medicinal plants, microorganisms and livestock. A total of around Rs 9.6 crore was received by the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) towards access to biological resources from users in various sectors during the period.Contributions were received by the NBA from both domestic and international entities, including companies from Sri Lanka, Germany, France, the Republic of Korea and Bhutan.Union environment ministry’s records show that the NBA has realised around Rs 278 crore through ABS and disbursed more than Rs 200 crore towards biodiversity conservation and benefits for communities, farmers, institutions and other benefit claimers across the country since 2008.The Authority, a statutory body under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, regulates access to India's biological resources and associated knowledge and implements the Nagoya Protocol’s (a global convention) principle of fair and equitable sharing of benefits.Biological resources, used by different entities for developing seeds, include livestock genetic resources such as Mithun, Jersey cattle and frozen semen of Murrah buffalo, as well as Red Sanders wood sourced from cultivated sources and auctioned material. The range further includes agricultural crops such as chickpea, red lentil, green moong, horse gram, flaxseed, guar gum, tapioca, buckwheat, brown rice, cauliflower, okra, hot pepper, brinjal and ridge gourd.The biological resources also include medicinal plants such as Ashwagandha, Shatavari, Kalmegh, Vasaka, Licorice, Arjuna, Bacopa, Gotukola and Moringa, as well as soil microorganisms including Azospirillum, Azotobacter, Bacillus, Rhizobium, Trichoderma and Metarhizium.The ABS mechanism goes beyond monetary collection by linking the utilisation of biological resources with biodiversity conservation, sustainable use and equitable sharing of benefits.“Funds disbursed through the State Biodiversity Boards and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils support conservation of biological resources, preparation and updation of People's Biodiversity Registers, strengthening of Biodiversity Management Committees, biodiversity research and documentation, and benefits to local communities and other benefit claimers,” said the Union environment ministry on working of the mechanism and utilisation of the collected money.ABS-funded activities can complement relevant govt schemes and programmes, particularly those promoting tribal welfare, sustainable livelihoods and natural-resource-based enterprises, such as the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN), Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission and Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana.“Such convergence can strengthen community-led conservation, sustainable utilisation of biological resources and livelihood opportunities, while leveraging existing institutional mechanisms,” said the ministry in a statement.India’s ABS framework supports Target 13 of the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework on the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilisation of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge, as well as Target 19 on resource mobilisation. The framework also contributes to relevant Sustainable Development Goals, including SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production), SDG 15 (Life on Land) and SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals), through biodiversity conservation, sustainable resource use, livelihood support and institutional collaboration.“As India prepares to participate in the seventeenth meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP 17), commencing on 19 October 2026 in Yerevan, Armenia, its ABS framework demonstrates the country’s continued commitment to biodiversity conservation, the sustainable use of biological resources and the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from their utilisation,” said the ministry.
Article Summary: The agri-seed sector accounted for the largest share of receipts from users of the country’s biological resources. A total of around Rs 9.6 crore was received by the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) towards access to biological resources from users in various sectors.

Article Title: Less-than-2-lane NH stretches shrink to 8% as high-speed corridors surge
Article Text:
India's national highway system has undergone remarkable enhancements, reducing two-lane stretches to only 8%.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view How do you feel about the reduction of less-than-two-lane highways in India? It's a positive change It's a negative change 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Barely 8% of the country’s 1.46 lakh km national highway (NH) network is now less than two lanes wide, compared with 2018-19, when such stretches accounted for nearly one-fourth of the network. Data shows the length of less-than-two-lane NHs has shrunk by 64% over the past nine years to around 13,000 km.In contrast, the length of high speed corridors (HSCs) has expanded more than 12-fold, while highways with four or more lanes have grown 1.5 times.Officials said the focus of highway development has increasingly shifted towards HSCs, greenfield access-controlled corridors and expressways. As these corridors are at least four lanes wide, their share in the overall NH network is expected to rise further. They said this would facilitate faster movement of passengers and freight while reducing logistics costs.However, despite the push for wider and seamless road connectivity, the average speed of trucks and the distance they cover each day remain well below global benchmarks. A truck in India typically covers only 300-350 km a day, compared with 700-800 km in the US and around 550-650 km in China.Officials said a comparison of truck speeds on two parallel highways illustrates the advantage of access-controlled corridors. On the Ahmedabad-Vadodara Expressway, trucks were found to travel at an average speed of around 80 kmph, compared with about 52 kmph on the parallel NH-64. The study also found that daily truck traffic on the expressway is nearly double that on the existing national highway.People aware of the govt’s plan to go for more HSCs said that the target is to build around 51,000 km of such network in the next 10 years, including the corridors developed or to be built by state govts.
Article Summary: Barely 8% of the country’s 1.46 lakh km national highway network is now less than two lanes wide. In 2018-19, such stretches accounted for nearly one-fourth of the network. Data shows the length of less-than-two-lane NHs has shrunk by 64% over the past nine years.

Article Title: Fuel tank cavities & Myanmar links: NCB busts 50 crores Yaba Haul, 2 Manipur residents arrested
Article Text:
The breakthrough comes as part of a wider, intensified crackdown on narcotics trafficking across the North Eastern region.

Acting on intelligence inputs, NCB smeuths intercepted two suspicious trucks in Guwahati.

In a blow to cross-border synthetic drug cartels, Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) intercepted a massive quantity of Yaba tablets sent to India from Myanmar and arrested two alleged traffickers who are resident of Manipur. The drugs are estimated to be worth Rs 50 crores in the international market."WY" methamphetamine refers to Yaba, a highly addictive combination of methamphetamine and caffeine pressed into pills. The tablets are usually orange or green and are frequently stamped with the letters "WY"."They typically contain a mixture of methamphetamine, caffeine, and binders. The term "Yaba" comes from the Thai word for "crazy medicine." The 'WY' stamp is widely associated with illicit production networks in the Golden Triangle region of Southeast Asia, particularly Myanmar," a senior officer said."Because it combines a potent central nervous system stimulant with caffeine, it causes intense stimulation, followed by a severe crash, addiction, and significant long-term physical and mental health risks," the official added.The breakthrough comes as part of a wider, intensified crackdown on narcotics trafficking across the North Eastern region.Acting on intelligence inputs, NCB smeuths intercepted two suspicious trucks in Guwahati.A search of the vehicles uncovered specially fabricated concealed cavities cleverly built inside the fuel tanks -- a sophisticated method designed to evade law enforcement checkpoints. Officers recovered the massive consignment of methamphetamine on the spot. Both arrested suspects are residents of Bishnupur, Manipur.Preliminary investigation revealed that the multi-crore drug consignment originated from Myanmar. The NCB is aggressively pursuing the wider network to identify international suppliers, domestic receivers, financiers, transporters, and other handlers to dismantle the entire supply chain from source to destination.The agency said the operation continues and it is committed to dismantling drug networks, tracking financial trails, and fulfilling the national vision of a Nasha Mukt Bharat (Drugs-Free India).Emphasizing a zero-tolerance approach, the NCB said its operational strategy extends far beyond individual seizures, prioritizing the destruction of financial and logistical syndicates."To combat the organized nature of these cartels, NCB Guwahati zone is maintaining coordinated intelligence-sharing with state police, the Anti-Narcotics Task Forces (ANTF), Assam Rifles, BSF, CRPF, SSB, Customs, DRI, NIA, and the Enforcement Directorate (ED)," an officer said.In a seperate operation, the NCB Guwahati zone concluded a targeted fortnight-long special drive aimed at apprehending long-standing fugitives in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) cases.The drive successfully tracked down six key accused evading the legal process. Of those captured, two are from Assam, while the remaining four hail from Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Manipur, and Tripura.Officials stated that the drive reinforces the agency's resolve to hunt down absconders across state borders, ensuring that pending cases reach logical conclusions through rigorous prosecution.
Article Summary: Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) intercepted massive quantity of Yaba tablets sent to India from Myanmar. The drugs are estimated to be worth Rs 50 crores in the international market. The breakthrough comes as part of a wider, intensified crackdown on narcotics trafficking across the North Eastern region.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday urged students in Chennai to develop innovative solutions to global challenges and carry Tamil culture wherever they go. Addressing the golden jubilee celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya Matriculation Higher Secondary School, he said the ideas of young Indians would shape the future of both the country and the world."The new ideas and solutions needed for a developed India will not only shape the future of India but also of the world. Today the world is looking for solutions, and you have the potential to provide these solutions. There is infinite opportunity in India today. I want every youth to see his future on the same big canvas because this is your time. This is your opportunity. I have full faith that this dream of ours will be fulfilled. Together we will do it," PM Modi said.The Prime Minister urged students to dream big, expand their horizons and pursue their ideas fearlessly. He expressed confidence that their efforts would help India achieve its goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047.The Prime Minister highlighted Tamil Nadu's cultural and spiritual heritage during his address. Referring to the first day of Navratri, he described his visit to the state and his interaction with students as a positive beginning to the auspicious occasion."Today marks the first day of Navratri—a sacred land of Shiva and Shakti. The privilege of visiting Tamil Nadu and the opportunity to meet the devotees of Goddess Saraswati make for a wonderful beginning to Navratri for me. I also witnessed the enthusiasm of my young friends; I can truly feel this positive energy and excitement," PM Modi added.He also praised the ancient Tamil classic Tirukkural, describing it as a valuable guide for those committed to learning throughout their lives. He recalled gifting the work to Russian President Vladimir Putin.Referring to his association with Kashi, his parliamentary constituency, PM Modi invoked Tamil poet Subramania Bharati's message of fearlessness. He encouraged students to act boldly, turn their ideas into action and remain open to new knowledge.PM Modi outlined India's ambitions, including becoming one of the world's three largest economies, emerging as a global manufacturing hub and sending an Indian to the Moon. He expressed confidence that collective efforts would help the country realise these goals.The Prime Minister also referred to India's sporting ambitions. He said the country was working towards hosting the 2030 Commonwealth Games and pursuing its ambition to stage the 2036 Olympic Games.The Prime Minister highlighted the expansion of higher education since 2014. He said the number of universities had increased from 750 to more than 1,300, while colleges had grown from 38,000 to over 52,000.He encouraged students to remain curious and continue learning, stressing the importance of education, innovation and new ideas in building a developed India.Earlier in the day, PM Modi said India's overall progress depended on the development of its states. He reaffirmed the Centre's focus on strengthening manufacturing, infrastructure and job creation, highlighting the role of Tamil Nadu in the country's industrial growth."We need to strengthen the states to strengthen the nation, and therefore, the central government is promoting manufacturing in states like Tamil Nadu. The campaigns of the central government, be it 'Make in India' or 'Vocal for Local', are benefiting Tamil Nadu as well," he said.The event marked 50 years of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya Matriculation Higher Secondary School and its contribution to education in Tamil Nadu.
Article Summary: PM Modi urged students to dream big, expand their horizons and pursue their ideas fearlessly. Article Title: 48 lakh calls in four years: India turns to Tele-MANAS as WHO flags mental healthcare gaps
Article Text:
Since its launch in October 2022, Tele-MANAS has received almost 48 lakh calls, highlighting a crucial demand for accessible mental health support.

NEW DELHI:

Exam stress, workplace pressure, anxiety, sleep problems and relationship difficulties are among the concerns for which people are turning to India’s national mental health helpline, Tele-MANAS, which has received nearly 48 lakh calls in four years. The figures offer a glimpse of the need for accessible mental health support, even as a new World Health Organization (WHO) guide warns that the global shift from hospital-centred care to community-based services remains far from complete.Released ahead of World Mental Health Day, the WHO guide found that 81% of countries continue to provide mental health services in psychiatric hospitals, while only 9% have completed the transition to community-based care. Another 53% remain at an early stage of the shift.The gap is particularly striking in the WHO South-East Asia region, where 63% of countries are still at an early stage of transition and none has completed it, according to the report’s regional assessment. The figures are regional and do not represent India’s individual status.The consequences of hospital-centred care are reflected in the duration of admissions.The report found that 28% of people admitted to psychiatric hospitals stay for more than six months, while 16% remain for over a year. It also estimates that 47% of mental health expenditure goes to psychiatric hospitals, although this figure is based on data from only 49 countries.The WHO calls for mental healthcare to be delivered closer to people’s homes, supported by community services, rehabilitation, housing and continued clinical care. It cautions that deinstitutionalisation cannot mean simply closing hospitals or discharging patients without follow-up. Without adequate planning and support, people risk being neglected or losing access to care.In India, Tele-MANAS has received 47,75,644 calls since its launch on October 10, 2022. Of the 13.35 lakh caller profiles analysed by the Union Health Ministry, 73.2% belonged to people aged 18-45.Men accounted for 54.18% of the profiles and women 43.78%.The free, confidential service is available round the clock on, through 53 operational cells covering all 36 States and Union Territories. The government has also sanctioned the District Mental Health Programme in 767 districts and integrated mental health services into more than 1.83 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: In 2012, Taylor Swift pledged $4 million for a Nashville education centre; 14 years later, the space is showcasing artwork by local schoolchildren and artists with developmental disabilities
Article Text:
Taylor Swift

A major gift for education

Taylor Swift’s ‘Patient Zero’ mansion: Inside the $47 million Beverly Hills home where her music video was filmed(Image Credit: Instagram)

Learning by making

Two groups, one exhibition

A centre still doing its job

From a pledge to a public platform

Taylor Swift’s $4 million gift to the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum in 2012 helped create a dedicated education centre in Nashville. The space was designed for more than music lessons: it would give children and families room to learn, experiment and engage with country music’s history. Fourteen years later, the centre is hosting Connection, an exhibition of posters created by Metro Nashville Public Schools students and artists from Friends Life Community, a nonprofit serving adults with developmental disabilities. The museum says the participants explored the history and techniques of Hatch Show Print, its historic letterpress shop, before making their own work. The exhibition brings the centre’s original educational promise to life, showing how a space built for learning can keep opening doors to creativity and community.In May 2012, Swift pledged $4 million towards a new education centre at the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum. According to MusicRow, it was the largest capital contribution by an individual artist in the museum’s 45-year history at the time. The museum named the centre in her honour.The gift formed part of a wider expansion campaign called 'Working on a Building: Country Music Lives Here'. The museum planned to grow from 140,000 square feet to more than 350,000 square feet, creating additional exhibition and learning spaces as well as new visitor facilities.The Taylor Swift Education Center was planned as a space of more than 7,500 square feet, spread across parts of two floors. Its design included three classrooms and a children’s exhibition gallery. The museum expected its new facilities to increase its educational capacity by as much as sevenfold.The planned classrooms were intended for a range of activities, from the museum’s flagship Words & Music programme to family events and distance learning. One “wet classroom” was designed for hands-on projects that could get messy, including letterpress art activities connected to Hatch Show Print.The centre’s original vision was not limited to traditional classroom instruction. The museum planned spaces where students could explore objects, observe curators at work and take part in activities that made music history tangible. A visible storage area and design studio would allow visitors to see how museum professionals handle and interpret collections.That hands-on approach is reflected in the centre’s current exhibition, Connection. Opened in 2026, the show brings together posters made by Metro Nashville Public Schools students and artists engaged with Friends Life Community. The project began with visits to Hatch Show Print, the museum’s nearly 150-year-old letterpress shop. Students learned about the shop’s history, studied design principles and explored how letterpress printing works. They then created shapes using foam and sponges, printed those forms and used them as inspiration for their finished posters, as per reports.The process gave participants a chance to learn not only by looking at art, but by making it. They experimented with words, images, colour and composition, using the print shop’s techniques to develop their own visual ideas.The exhibition also grew from a collaboration between the museum and Friends Life Community, which serves adults with developmental disabilities. Friends Life invited Hatch Show Print Master Printer Emeritus Jim Sherraden to work as a teaching artist in residence in 2023. In late 2024, artists from Friends Life Community visited the print shop for a behind-the-presses tour. Sherraden and Jennifer Haston, the organisation’s visual arts programme coordinator, helped participants bring their words, lettering and images to life through poster-making, as per reports.The posters created by both groups form the exhibition’s central focus. The museum says the works use action words and imagery to imagine a future where people connect through creative art and social causes. The title Connection speaks to the ideas behind the exhibition, but also to the relationships built through the process: between students and artists, participants and printers, and the public and the museum.The project demonstrates how a museum education space can bring people together across ages and abilities. It also gives visitors the opportunity to encounter work made by members of their own community, rather than only by established artists or historical figures.When Swift made her pledge, the museum described the centre as a place for school groups, families, young people and adults. The new exhibition shows how that original ambition continues to shape the space more than a decade later.The education centre is not simply a room named after a famous musician. It is part of the museum’s broader effort to connect people with country music and its creative traditions through participation. In Connection, that means learning about letterpress printing, trying the process and producing posters that reflect the creators’ own ideas.The exhibition is open to museum visitors, with admission included in the price of a museum ticket. The museum also offers free admission for local youth and discounted tickets for up to two accompanying adults from Davidson County and neighbouring counties, with proof of residency.Swift’s generous contribution of $4 million played a crucial role in creating a lasting educational component within one of Nashville’s most iconic cultural institutions. The carefully designed classrooms, a dedicated children’s gallery, and interactive programming were all put in place with the intention of transforming the museum into more than just a location for viewing exhibitions. These elements were strategically crafted to provide visitors with opportunities to learn through hands-on experiences and active participation.Fast forward a remarkable fourteen years, and the vibrant and eye-catching posters showcased in the current exhibition, aptly titled Connection, stand as a compelling testament to that original vision which has been successfully brought to life. Local students, in collaboration with talented artists who have developmental disabilities, have engaged deeply in the exploration of a historic printing tradition. They have successfully harnessed this medium to express and convey their unique perspectives and personal narratives.However, it is important to note that this exhibition does not represent the conclusion of the center's evolving narrative. Instead, it serves to illustrate the extraordinary outcomes that can arise when a cultural institution commits resources and efforts toward creating a dedicated physical space, fostering educational opportunities, and promoting creative accessibility over an extended timeframe. A generous gift made in 2012 laid a solid foundation for establishing this creative setting; now, the individuals who engage with it today are actively populating that environment with their own creative works, innovative ideas, and meaningful connections.What are your views on this? Tell us in the comments section below.
Article Summary: In May 2012, Swift pledged $4 million towards a new education centre at the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum in Nashville. Fourteen years later, the centre is hosting Connection, an exhibition of posters created by Metro Nashville Public Schools students and artists from Friends Life Community.

Article Title: Delhi Rains: Delhi-NCR wakes up to heavy rain, thunderstorms; IMD issues red alert
Article Text:
Delhi experienced heavy rain and thunderstorms on Monday morning, leading to a noticeable change in weather





NEW DELHI: Heavy rain and thunderstorms swept across Delhi on Monday morning, bringing cooler conditions to the national capital and causing waterlogging near Jhandewalan Temple in the Karol Bagh area.The India Meteorological Department (IMD) warned of moderate to heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms over Delhi-NCR for the next two to three hours.“Moderate to heavy rainfall accompanied with thunderstorm likely over Delhi-NCR during the next 2-3 hours,” the weather department said.The morning showers brought a change in weather conditions, with overcast skies across the region. However, the IMD's forecast indicates that the wet spell is unlikely to continue through the week, with partly cloudy skies and no rainfall predicted over the next several days.Maximum temperatures are expected to remain between 31 and 35 degrees Celsius, while minimum temperatures are likely to hover between 22 and 25 degrees Celsius.The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for Delhi, warning of thunderstorms, lightning, gusty winds of around 60 kmph and heavy rainfall across all 11 districts of the national capital until 9am on Monday.An orange alert has been issued for parts of Haryana and Uttar Pradesh.According to the seven-day forecast issued on Sunday evening, the maximum temperature on October 13 is expected to range between 32 and 34 degrees Celsius, with the minimum between 23 and 25 degrees Celsius. Article Title: In 2022, Ryan Reynolds and Blake Lively gave $500,000 to Water First; four years later, the Canadian charity's latest graduating class included eight newly certified Indigenous water operators
Article Text:
(Instagram)

A donation aimed at local training

Eight new operators graduate

Why local operators matter

A continuing water challenge

Building skills for the long term

In 2022, Ryan Reynolds and Blake Lively donated $500,000 to Water First, a Canadian charity that works with Indigenous communities on water education and training. Four years later, the organisation marked a milestone: eight Indigenous trainees had graduated from a 15-month programme as certified water operators. The graduates completed more than 2,000 hours of hands-on training and passed the exams required for certification, according to Water First. Their achievement points to the long-term purpose of the 2022 gift, which was intended to help more Indigenous young adults train for water-related careers. The donation did not solve Canada’s drinking-water challenges on its own, but it supported a locally focused approach: building skills so communities can strengthen their own capacity to manage water systems.When Reynolds and Lively announced their donation in March 2022, they said it would support Water First’s education and training programmes for Indigenous youth and young adults. The funds were intended to help train water treatment plant operators and environmental water science technicians, as well as introduce school-aged students to water science. Reynolds described access to clean drinking water as a basic human right and said the couple valued Water First’s focus on training Indigenous adults to become certified operators and technicians.Their contribution supported a charity that works alongside communities to develop programmes shaped by local priorities, rather than relying on a single, identical solution for every place, as per the report.Water First says its partnerships are built around collaboration with Indigenous communities. Local leaders help identify needs and shape the training, with the goal of developing expertise within the communities themselves. That approach recognises that the challenges facing one water system may differ from those affecting another.The need for trained local operators is one part of a wider picture. Communities can face issues involving infrastructure, water quality or a shortage of people qualified to operate treatment systems. Training does not replace necessary equipment or investment, but it can help communities build the people and knowledge needed to manage water systems over the long term.The latest group of graduates completed a Drinking Water Internship run through a partnership between Water First, the Anishinaabeg of Kabapikotawangag Resource Council, participating communities and Big Island First Nation. The eight graduates celebrated their achievement in May 2026. The 15-month programme combined classroom learning with practical experience. Each intern completed more than 2,000 hours of hands-on training and wrote four exams required to earn Water Operator certification. The work prepared participants for the responsibilities involved in operating drinking-water treatment systems. The graduates are now equipped to pursue careers in water treatment and related environmental fields. Their training can also benefit their communities directly, particularly where local residents are needed to operate and maintain water facilities.One graduate, Brandon Penner of Big Grassy First Nation, said the programme pushed him beyond his comfort zone and helped him recognise what he could achieve through commitment. He also spoke of a deep connection to the natural world and a desire to protect it for future generations.For many communities, having trained local people involved in water management can make a difference to both daily operations and long-term self-sufficiency. Water First’s announcement quoted Rhonda Nash, director of operations at AKRC, saying that certified operators were needed for the council’s five member First Nations, which include seven separate communities, two of them remote. Nash said the goal was to ensure access to clean drinking water while creating employment and enabling community members to operate their own treatment plants. The model links technical training with local jobs and community capacity.That work is important because water systems require skilled people to monitor processes, respond to problems and maintain consistent operations. The graduates’ certification gives them a professional foundation, while their local knowledge and relationships can help connect technical work with community needs.Water First says its internship alumni can also access continuing career development and education through an expanding professional network. That support matters because training is not a one-time event. Operators may need ongoing learning as their responsibilities grow and water-management challenges change.The graduation comes amid persistent drinking-water concerns in Indigenous communities across Canada. Water First’s May 2026 release said 16% of First Nations were affected by a drinking-water advisory, with the figure rising to 32% in Ontario. The charity cautioned that the issue is complex, involving different combinations of infrastructure, source-water quality and staffing needs.Those figures help explain why the organisation focuses on partnerships and locally designed programmes. No single intervention can address every cause of unsafe or unreliable water. Communities may need infrastructure improvements, source-water protection, technical expertise and sustained funding, often at the same time.Water First frames training as one part of the solution, not a substitute for broader action. Developing local expertise can help communities operate systems and strengthen their ability to respond to challenges, while wider infrastructure and policy needs remain.The eight new operators are part of a growing network. Water First reported that 73 interns from 47 Indigenous communities had graduated from its internship programmes to date, logging approximately 170,000 hours working in local water plants and attending workshops.Those numbers represent more than training hours. They reflect the development of experience that can remain within communities and support future generations. A certified operator can help a community manage a water system today, while also becoming a mentor or resource for others pursuing similar work.Reynolds and Lively’s $500,000 donation helped Water First expand its capacity to offer hands-on training to more Indigenous youth and adults. Four years later, the graduation of eight operators shows one concrete outcome of that broader effort. The donation was one contribution among many, alongside funding from government programmes, community partnerships and other supporters.The water challenges facing Indigenous communities are far from resolved. But the new graduates represent an important step towards local capacity, skilled employment and stronger community involvement in water management. Their certification gives them tools to protect a resource that communities depend on every day, and helps keep the work of building a more sustainable future close to home. Their progress also shows how sustained training and community partnerships can help turn support into lasting change.
Article Summary: Eight Indigenous trainees have graduated from a 15-month programme as certified water operators. The graduates completed more than 2,000 hours of hands-on training and passed the exams required for certification. Their achievement points to the long-term purpose of the 2022 gift, intended to help more Indigenous young adults train for water-related careers.

Article Title: After tragedy at Satya Niketan, 30 illegal, dangerous buildings razed daily
Article Text:
Municipal Corporation of Delhi has taken strict action against illegal constructions following a serious building collapse.

From September 6 to October 10, over 1,000 properties were demolished across twelve zones.





NEW DELHI: Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) demolished at least 30 properties daily from Sept 6 to Oct 10 in a crackdown on illegal and dangerous buildings after the collapse of a paying guest accomodation in Satya Niketan killed seven people.According to govt data released Sunday, the corporation demolished 1,046 properties across its 12 zones, sealed 282 properties, and pulled down 47 dangerous buildings.Chief minister Rekha Gupta earlier directed MCD to intensify its demolition drive against illegal structures and dangerous buildings across all zones.Among the 12 zones, the maximum demolition action was recorded in Rohini (158 properties), followed by South (121) and Shahdara North (115). City-SP, West and Shahdara South zones saw action against 87 properties each, closely followed by Karol Bagh with 85. The remaining zones included Central, where action was taken against 75 properties; Civil Lines (63), Keshavpuram (61), Najafgarh (45) and Narela (62).Of the sealed properties, 87 were in City-SP zone, 41 in Shahdara North and South, 27 in Shahdara South, while 23 were in the Central zone.Karol Bagh accounted for 13 of the 47 dangerous buildings demolished.Civil Lines, City-SP and West zones reported eight each, while Narela, Rohini, Keshavpuram and South had two each. Shahdara South and Najafgarh reported one each.Following a building collapse in Seemapuri, one unsafe building was demolished and Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board issued notices to three other houses.Gupta said the campaign would continue, adding that agencies must act according to rules in cases involving illegal construction and unsafe buildings.
Article Summary: From September 6 to October 10, over 1,000 properties were demolished across twelve zones. Chief minister Rekha Gupta earlier directed MCD to intensify its demolition drive against illegal structures and dangerous buildings. Rohini (158 properties), followed by South (121) and Shahdara North (115)

Article Title: RBI measures see sharp impact as rupee rises 1% against US dollar; what steps were announced?
Article Text:
The rupee has recovered sharply following the RBI's announcement.

RBI announces measures for rupee

The rupee gained a stunning 1% at the start of trading on Monday after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) eased pressure on the currency by shifting oil companies' dollar purchases away from the spot market and taking steps to curb corporate demand for forward dollars.The rupee began Monday’s session at 95.76 against the US dollar, compared with its Friday closing level of 96.73.In fact, it emerged as one of Asia's strongest-performing currencies, even as most regional currencies moved within a narrow range. Despite Monday's sharp rise, the rupee has lost 6.6% against the dollar so far this year, according to a Reuters report.Also Read | RBI has record forex reserves, but why is rupee still not out of the woods?On Saturday, the RBI announced a set of measures targeting two major sources of pressure on the rupee. These include sustained dollar purchases by oil marketing companies amid elevated crude prices and demand from corporates looking to protect themselves against further currency depreciation.Fears of additional weakness in the rupee had prompted importers to increase their purchases of forward dollars to shield themselves from potentially higher costs in the future.However, the increased demand for hedging also put further pressure on the currency.This created a cycle in which expectations of depreciation encouraged more hedging, adding to the rupee's weakness and reinforcing those expectations.Among the measures announced by the RBI were a ban on companies rebooking cancelled rupee-linked derivatives, a reduction in the threshold for transactions that do not have an underlying exposure, and a requirement for banks to maintain a 20% cash reserve against certain foreign-exchange contracts. These steps could make hedging against a weaker rupee more expensive.Citi said in a note that the package increases the immediate cost of trades aimed at benefiting from rupee depreciation.Bankers clarified that the restrictions do not cover every foreign-exchange transaction and apply only to current account transactions.The 20% cash requirement also excludes companies hedging external commercial borrowings and foreign portfolio investors seeking to hedge their investments in India.The rupee has recovered sharply following the RBI's announcement, but analysts believe the durability of the gains will depend on whether the underlying pressures on the currency begin to ease."Beyond the initial impact, the rupee’s trajectory will continue to be shaped by crude oil prices, foreign portfolio flows and the broader direction of the US dollar," Societe Generale said in a note.
Article Summary: The rupee gained a stunning 1% at the start of trading on Monday. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) eased pressure on the currency by shifting oil companies' dollar purchases away from the spot market. The rupee began Monday’s session at 95.76 against the US dollar, compared with its Friday closing level of 96.73.

Article Title: Watch: Men in nighties, masks loot SBI ATM in Telangana; Rs 25 lakh suspected stolen
Article Text:
Three men allegedly broke into a State Bank of India ATM in Gandhari mandal using a gas cutter.





HYDERABAD: Three men wearing nighties and masks allegedly broke into a State Bank of India (SBI) ATM in Gandhari mandal headquarters in the early hours of Sunday and fled with cash after cutting open the machine with a gas cutter.Police suspect that around Rs 25 lakh may have been stolen, though the exact amount is yet to be confirmed.According to police, the three unidentified men arrived at the ATM centre in a vehicle shortly after 1 am on Sunday. While one of them stood guard outside, the other two entered the centre and used a gas cutter to break open the ATM. They then took the cash and fled.The theft came to light on Sunday morning when locals noticed the damaged ATM and alerted the police. Police reached the spot and collected details about the incident.Police are examining CCTV footage from the ATM centre and surrounding areas to identify the suspects and trace their movements. Footage from cameras inside the centre reportedly captured two men in nighties cutting open the ATM and fleeing with the cash. Their identities and the place from which they arrived are yet to be established.Gandhari police station sub-inspector M Mahender said preliminary information suggests that the ATM operators deposited around Rs 30 lakh into the machine at about 1 pm on Friday.Customers are believed to have withdrawn around Rs 5 lakh by midnight on Saturday, leaving approximately Rs 25 lakh in the machine. Police suspect that the remaining amount was taken by the gang, but the exact cash loss has not yet been established.
